svg.title: AdoSQL - Detailed architecture
svg.desc: Proposed multi-organization ADO ingestion, normalized SQL data, SKU-to-media/platform mapping, deterministic metrics and grounded LLM issue summaries displayed in the dashboard's rightmost column.
svg.text: Eight ADO stages -> normalized evidence -> SKU mapping -> dashboard + LLM insights
Fixed stage order | each stage has its own ADO organization.
ADO Analytics / APIs: work items, links and evidence
Normalize stage records and issue records
Standardize field names, entities, states and timestamps
Preserve source org / project / work item provenance
Deduplicate by source identity, not title
Common evidence captured for all 8 stages
Media / platform / SKU identity + stage + test run
Test start date / end date + sign-off owner / status
Issue ID, description, state and category
StageTest, Issue, Report, SignOff and Entity records
Canonical identity: organization + project + work item ID
Keep repeat test runs and source links traceable
Proposed normalized model extends this foundation
Resolve all applicable stage evidence per SKU
Media: CDL + RDT + Media Perf testing
SKU: SKU Qual + Scale Test + Load & Performance Test
SKU composition and canonical entity IDs
Approved mappings; never guess joins from names
Link applicable components, stages and test runs
Do not invent associations or mark missing tests passed
Build the SKU-level SQL evidence view
Unique issue counts by stage / theme and internal / external
Test dates, sign-off owners, reports, exceptions and coverage
Issue durations from timestamps; missing data stays unknown
Count each source issue once per SKU
Resolved duration = resolution time - start time
Open issue age = refresh time - start time
Issue-days are not elapsed test duration
Generate and validate the LLM summary
Ground in the SKU's mapped evidence and SQL counts
Explain media / platform / load issue themes
Cite source ADO items and test reports
Do not invent counts, sign-offs or root causes
SKU dashboard | illustrative output, not live test data
Dashboard drill-through: SKU -> stage / test run -> issue, report, sign-off and exception evidence.
Proposed architecture: extends the repo's single-organization C# ADO-to-SQL sync; no claim that the full dashboard or LLM exists today.
Secrets stay outside code. Retain source provenance and refresh status; do not confuse missing evidence with zero issues.
